title: Recordings with Baby Dodds, George Lewis and Rudi Blesh; Babe's party jobs
summary: Bernice recalls recording with Rudi Blesh, Baby Dodds and George Lewis, and George's mother's illness. Babe got jobs for George and others playing picnics and parties for white engineers, with John Casimir (clarinet) as a later sideman.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So you made some records, huh? Yeah, I made records with Rudy Blair and Baby Dodge and George Lewis. You known Joey's finished a good while? Oh yes, indeed. We were like a family. That's why I don't understand why he didn't call here to let me know his mother had passed. I know he came here. He said, I wasn't going to leave out of town until I come see you. He said, his mother, every time he got ready to go somewhere to see somebody, she'd make out she's sick. I said, no, George, she's old and she ain't been seeing you much. And I said, she just wants you around. He said, oh, she just be putting on for you. He said, I can't stay up under. I've got to get out and look for money. So I said, he said, well, she fell. He said, I just told her stay in bed. He said, I didn't get no doctor or nothing. I told her stay in the bed and I rubbed her and I'll give her some kind of medicine. He said, give her. I said, well, if I was on my feet, I'd go there and see about her. He said, she'd be all right if she'd be up the next day or so. That's right. That's what it is. And my mind belonged to them people. I said, I'm going to call. And I said, no, I'll wait. With Krishna Baby, I said, I'm going to call Derek and tell him with Krishna Baby. I said, no, he'll call me. And no later than die. I don't know. Did Babe work with him much? Oh yeah, they played music a lot. They used to play. For all them white people, all the U.S. engineers, Babe would get the jobs and George and him sign them up, you know, picnics, weddings, and any kind of party they'd give, they'd see Babe. Babe would get pajo too. The last one he had, he had pajo on him because George was out of town. And he got another fella. What is his name? Henry, ain't he? He lived around there with played with his daddy. John. John. What instrument did he play? John. John, he played a horn. John Cajmy. Yeah, well I know John Cajmy. He's a clarinet player.

Yeah. My baby used to get him jobs too. He's the one that had the young tuxedo draft. Yeah, uh-huh. Yeah, that's him. When I may see him Tuesday, he's supposed to have a little funeral. Hmm? He's supposed to have a funeral Tuesday. Yeah, why? Up at the merry-go-round, Eagle and Hickory, you know? Oh yeah, you go where up there? Oh, anywhere I go in. I follow my job. Anytime there's any kind of music I like to hear. In my children come to me, they got some white

people down there following. I said, well, they always follow the band. You see, I don't believe they're from here. They look too nice to be from here. I said, one of them spoke to me just as nice. I said, well, they get from here then. Y'all were down there by the field down the street.
